# xapir<img src="man/figures/xapir.png" width="120px" align="right" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: Experimental](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/figures/lifecycle-experimental.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/Ivey-Business-School/xapir/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Ivey-Business-School/xapir/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/Ivey-Business-School/xapir/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/Ivey-Business-School/xapir)
<!-- badges: end -->

xapir reads from and writes to X through the X API v2, for students
learning about social media and marketing. You pull posts with one
function, save what comes back as a file, and unfold that file into
tidy tables with a second set of functions that never touch the API.
X bills every post it returns, so each reader tells you the most a call
can cost before it makes a request.

## Installation

The package is not on CRAN. Install a numbered release from GitHub:

```{r install}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Ivey-Business-School/xapir@v0.2.0")
```

If something goes wrong, file a small reproducible example on
[GitHub](https://github.com/Ivey-Business-School/xapir/issues).

## Authentication

Put two values from your app on the [X developer
portal](https://developer.x.com/en/portal/dashboard) in your `.Renviron`
file (`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens it), then restart R:

```
X_BEARER_TOKEN=AAAA...
X_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
```

The bearer token reads public data: timelines, searches, profiles, lists
and trends. Every reader picks it up from the environment; you never pass
it by hand.

The client id is for acting as yourself: the write functions and the
readers that only make sense for the signed-in account (`get_bookmark()`,
`get_liked_posts()`, `get_my_user()` and the like). The first such call
opens a browser window to approve the app. The token is then cached under
`httr2::oauth_cache_path()` in a folder named `xapir`, so you sign in
once, not every session. Delete that folder to sign in as someone else.

Two things must be true for that sign-in to work. The app's settings on
the developer portal must list `http://localhost:1410` as a callback URL,
exactly, or X's authorize page fails with "Something went wrong" and no
detail. And R must be interactive; from `Rscript` or a scheduled job,
set `options(rlang_interactive = TRUE)` first, or sign in once from
RStudio so the cached token is there for the job.

## What a call costs

X bills a read per item returned and a write per request. The prices
below are from the [pricing
page](https://docs.x.com/x-api/getting-started/pricing) on 24 September
2026; fields and expansions are free.

| Per item read                       | US$   |
|-------------------------------------|-------|
| post                                | 0.005 |
| user                                | 0.010 |
| follower or followed account        | 0.010 |
| list                                | 0.005 |
| space or community                  | 0.005 |
| user who liked, muted or blocked    | 0.001 |

| Per request                                                | US$   |
|------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| create a post                                              | 0.015 |
| create a post whose text carries a URL                     | 0.200 |
| post count, last seven days                                | 0.005 |
| post count, full archive                                   | 0.010 |
| trends                                                     | 0.010 |
| like, follow, repost, block or mute                        | 0.015 |
| undo one of those                                          | 0.010 |
| create a list                                              | 0.010 |
| change a list or its members; pin, follow or unfollow it   | 0.005 |
| bookmark or remove one; delete a post; hide a reply        | 0.005 |

Counts are not free, but a count is billed once however many posts it
covers, so it is still the cheap way to size a query. Before its first
request every reader prints the most it can spend, a paged reader prints
what it actually read at the end, and every write prints its price:

```
#> Reading up to 500 posts, about $2.50. Set max_posts to change this.
#> Finished getting posts on page 1
#> Read 143 posts, about $0.72.
#> This request costs about $0.015.
```

`max_posts` and `max_users` must be finite, and the last page is trimmed
so a pull never holds more than the cap. A `username` costs one user read
to become an id; pass `user_id` where a reader takes it to skip that.

Your own data is cheaper. X bills your own posts, mentions, likes,
bookmarks, followers, lists, blocks and mutes at US$0.001 an item when
the account that signed in owns the app. The package prices a read that
way when it knows the account is yours: the readers of the signed-in
account always, and the readers that take a `user_id` when that id is
yours. After a sign-in the package knows your id; before one, tell it
with `options(xapir.my_user_id = "<your id>")` in `.Rprofile`.

Two rules from the pricing page soften the bill. Reads are de-duplicated
within a UTC day: reading the same post twice on the same day is billed
once. And pay-per-use is capped at 3 million post reads a month.

Every price lives in one table. If X changes one, set
`options(xapir.prices = list(posts = 0.006))` in your `.Rprofile` and
every message follows; the older `xapir.price_per_post` and
`xapir.price_per_user` options still work.

## Read, save, unfold

```{r read-save-unfold}
library(xapir)

# Read: one pull, capped, over a window
timeline <- get_timeline(
  username   = "Tesla",
  max_posts  = 500,
  start_time = iso_8601("2026-01-01"),
  end_time   = iso_8601("2026-02-01")
)

# Save the raw pull before you touch it. Reading it back is free.
saveRDS(timeline, "tesla-2026-01.rds")
timeline <- readRDS("tesla-2026-01.rds")

# Unfold it into tables. None of these calls the API.
post       <- extract_post(timeline)
user       <- extract_user(timeline)
post_media <- extract_post_media(timeline)
post_url   <- extract_post_url(timeline)

# The tables join on post_id
library(dplyr)
post |>
  inner_join(post_media, by = "post_id") |>
  filter(type == "video") |>
  arrange(desc(view_count))
```

## The twelve tables

Each `extract_*()` function reads a saved pull and returns one table with
the same columns every time, even when it has no rows. Eleven join to the
post table on `post_id`; `extract_user()` joins on `user_id`. By default
each table includes the posts a timeline quotes, replies to or reposts;
pass `include_referenced_posts = FALSE` to keep only the posts the
endpoint returned. The post table has 24 columns (`paid_partnership` and
`community_id` are new in 0.2.0) and the user table 24 (`media_count`,
`verified_followers_count`, `subscription_type`, `parody`,
`profile_banner_url` and `pinned_post_id` are new).

| Function                           | One row per                       |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| `extract_post()`                   | post: text, counts, type, URL     |
| `extract_user()`                   | user: handle, bio, follower counts|
| `extract_post_media()`             | photo, video or GIF on a post     |
| `extract_post_url()`               | link in a post, with its preview  |
| `extract_post_mention()`           | account mentioned in a post       |
| `extract_post_hashtag()`           | hashtag in a post                 |
| `extract_post_cashtag()`           | cashtag in a post                 |
| `extract_post_context()`           | topic X assigned to a post        |
| `extract_post_entity_annotation()` | named entity X found in a post    |
| `extract_post_poll_option()`       | option of a poll on a post        |
| `extract_post_place()`             | post tagged with a place          |
| `extract_post_edited_post_id()`    | earlier version of an edited post |

## Readers

Every post reader returns the list of pages the tables above unfold; the
rest return a tibble directly. Readers marked "sign-in" use the user
token, the rest the bearer token.

| Function                                     | Returns                                            |
|----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| **Reading posts**                            |                                                    |
| `get_timeline(username = , user_id = )`      | an account's posts                                 |
| `get_recent_post(query)`                     | posts matching a search, last seven days           |
| `get_recent_post_count(query)`               | how many posts matched, per period                 |
| `get_post(post_ids)`                         | up to 100 posts by id                              |
| `get_quote_post(post_id)`                    | posts that quote a post                            |
| `get_repost(post_id)`                        | reposts of a post                                  |
| `get_mentions(username)`                     | posts that name an account                         |
| `get_account_timeline(username)`             | your home timeline (sign-in)                       |
| `get_bookmark()`                             | your bookmarks (sign-in)                           |
| `get_liked_posts(username)`                  | posts an account liked (sign-in)                   |
| `get_liking_users(post_id)`                  | users who liked a post, as a table (sign-in)       |
| `get_repost_of_me()`                         | your posts that were reposted (sign-in)            |
| `iso_8601(x)`                                | a date as the API wants it                         |
| **Accounts and follows**                     |                                                    |
| `get_users_by_usernames(usernames)`          | profiles by handle                                 |
| `get_users_by_ids(user_ids)`                 | profiles by id                                     |
| `search_users(query)`                        | profiles matching a search (sign-in)               |
| `get_followers(username = , user_id = )`     | who follows an account                             |
| `get_following(username = , user_id = )`     | who an account follows                             |
| `get_reposted_by(post_id)`                   | who reposted a post                                |
| `get_blocking()`                             | accounts you block (sign-in)                       |
| `get_muting()`                               | accounts you mute (sign-in)                        |
| **Lists**                                    |                                                    |
| `get_owned_list(username = , user_id = )`    | lists an account owns                              |
| `get_followed_lists(username = , user_id = )`| lists an account follows                           |
| `get_list_memberships(username = , user_id = )` | lists an account was added to                   |
| `get_pinned_lists()`                         | lists you pinned (sign-in)                         |
| `get_list_by_id(list_id)`                    | one list                                           |
| `get_list_member(list_id)`                   | the members of a list                              |
| `get_list_followers(list_id)`                | who follows a list                                 |
| `get_list_posts(list_id)`                    | the posts on a list, as pages                      |
| **Search the archive** (pay-per-use or Enterprise) |                                              |
| `get_all_post(query)`                        | posts matching a search, back to 2006, as pages    |
| `get_all_post_count(query)`                  | how many posts matched, per period                 |
| **Spaces, communities and news**             |                                                    |
| `get_spaces(space_ids = , user_ids = )`      | spaces by id or by creator                         |
| `search_spaces(query)`                       | live or scheduled spaces matching a search         |
| `get_space_posts(space_id)`                  | the posts shared in a space, as a page             |
| `get_community(community_id)`                | one community                                      |
| `search_communities(query)`                  | communities matching a search (sign-in)            |
| `search_news(query)`                         | news stories X built from posts                    |
| `get_news(news_id)`                          | one news story                                     |
| `get_trends_by_woeid(woeid)`                 | trending topics for a place                        |
| **Your own account**                         |                                                    |
| `get_my_user()`                              | your own profile (sign-in)                         |
| `get_usage()`                                | posts read this month against your cap             |
| `get_usage_credits()`                        | the dollar balance left on your account            |
| `get_post_analytics(post_ids, start_time, end_time)` | impressions, engagements and clicks on your posts (sign-in) |
| `get_personalized_trends()`                  | the trends X picks for you (sign-in)               |

User readers return the same 24 user columns as `extract_user()`; list
readers return eight list columns (`list_id`, `list_name`, ...).

## Writing to X

Each of these acts as the account that signed in, prints its price
before the request, returns the `data` block the API sends back
invisibly, and stops with the message X gives when the request is
refused.

```{r write}
new_post <- create_post(text = "Hello from R!")
#> This request costs about $0.015.
delete_post(post_ids = new_post$id)

# A photo: upload it first, then post with the id it returns
media_id <- upload_media("chart.png", alt_text = "Sales by month")
create_post(text = "Our year so far", media_ids = media_id)

# A reply, a quote, a poll
create_post(text = "Agreed!", reply_to_post_id = new_post$id)
create_post(text = "Worth a read", quote_post_id = "1234567890123456789")
create_post(text = "Which one?", poll_options = c("This", "That"))

like_post(post_id = "1234567890123456789")
unlike_post(post_id = "1234567890123456789")
create_repost(post_id = "1234567890123456789")
delete_repost(post_id = "1234567890123456789")
create_bookmark(post_id = "1234567890123456789")
delete_bookmark(post_id = "1234567890123456789")

follow_user(source_username = "your_handle", target_username = "XDevelopers")
unfollow_user(source_username = "your_handle", target_username = "XDevelopers")
mute_user(source_username = "your_handle", target_username = "XDevelopers")
unmute_user(source_username = "your_handle", target_username = "XDevelopers")
block_user(target_username = "spammer")
unblock_user(target_username = "spammer")
hide_reply(reply_id = "1234567890123456789")

# Lists: create, fill, pin, delete
new_list <- create_list(name = "EV makers")
add_list_member(list_id = new_list$id, username = "Tesla")
pin_list(list_id = new_list$id)
delete_list(list_id = new_list$id)
```

One gotcha: a post whose text carries a URL costs $0.200, not $0.015.
The price line printed before the request shows which rate applies, so
read it before posting a batch with links.

## What is not covered

Streaming, webhooks, the Activity API, direct messages, Chat,
Broadcasts, Community Notes, Compliance, Bots and Articles. The package
covers what a marketing course reads and writes, not the whole API.

The [Getting Started](https://Ivey-Business-School.github.io/xapir/articles/getting-started.html)
guide walks through all of this, and the
[reference index](https://Ivey-Business-School.github.io/xapir/reference/index.html)
lists every function with its arguments and columns.
